clue.text: Conjuror's skill lacking punch, according to report?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the clue's phrase is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a fist without punch is a weak, flimsy hand: 'slight of hand' read literally

explanation.surface: A magician whose act has lost its impact, according to the reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking punch' is a whimsical 'slight of hand', a feeble fist, which is said the same as the conjuror's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual dexterity used to fool an audience is the core skill of a stage magician.

clue.text: Youthful figure to pounce on coward

parts.note: to spring is to leap or pounce on prey
a chicken is slang for a coward

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a young person to jump on a timid fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no spring chicken' describes someone no longer young, so the phrase itself means a youngster.

clue.text: Active mooring in city is well-designed for users

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the abbreviation for the City of London

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London, the financial district

indicators.note: active suggests the letters are lively and stirring, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Busy berthing of boats in a town is designed well for the people who use it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Active' looks like part of the mooring picture but is the anagram signal; the city is the City of London, known by its postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomics is the study of fitting equipment to the people who use it, so a comfortable, efficient design qualifies.

clue.text: Form of therapy gets perverted by a military officer

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lt is the standard abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A treatment regime is corrupted by an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' rearranges GETS to GEST, followed by A and LT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestalt therapy is a recognised school of psychotherapy focused on present awareness.

clue.text: Attempts to limit British factions

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in or contain, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Efforts are made to restrain partisan groups within Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribes in the loose sense are groups bound by shared loyalty, much like factions or clans.

clue.text: Wonderful football organisation almost broke? See United coming in

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football

indicators.note: coming in means arriving inside, so these letters are placed within the shortened word
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bust means broke, penniless
lo is an old word meaning see! or behold!
U is a standard abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A great football body nearly bankrupt? Look at Manchester United joining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the word for broke, and 'coming in' places the see-and-United pair inside what remains; 'See' is the old exclamation, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous is an everyday synonym for marvellous or terrific.

clue.text: Expressing romance or love between two Americans

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle of the two other pieces

parts.note: AM is short for American
US is short for American, as in the United States
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance or affection blossoming between a pair of Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two Americans' gives two abbreviations, AM and US, and 'between' puts OR plus O in the middle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means showing sexual or romantic desire, so it expresses romance.

clue.text: Germany's fairy-folk, running short? Search deeply

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

indicators.note: running short means coming up one letter shy, so the last is dropped

parts.note: elves are fairy-folk of folklore

explanation.surface: Germany's mythical little people are running out of time to hunt for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig or research thoroughly.

clue.text: Artist's chatter: Indian music

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A painter's small talk is about music from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragas are the melodic frameworks of classical music in South Asia.

clue.text: I go limbo dancing round King, causing confusion

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
dancing letters jig about, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Doing the limbo around the monarch causes a mix-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges I GO LIMBO, and 'round' wraps those letters around R.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a complicated, confused situation or entanglement.

clue.text: See 27 Across
A porn line, though nasty, is unparalleled

indicators.note: nasty suggests something spoilt or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smutty line, however offensive, is beyond compare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges all of A PORN LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonpareil is something without equal, so the adjective means peerless.

clue.text: Some particular epoch recalled in musical work

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the run is read backwards
some means a portion only, so the letters are found within the words

explanation.surface: Part of a certain era remembered in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes AREPO from particulAR EPOch, and 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music.

clue.text: Was worth a little time in minor acting role

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a cameo is a brief appearance by an actor
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An actor was paid for a short spell in a walk-on part.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that came to ten pounds totalled, or amounted to, that sum.

clue.text: Take action about new climb in good weather

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
to shin is to climb, as up a pole

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stand on a fresh ascent in fine conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the legal-action word around the new-plus-climb pair; 'Take action' reads as a call to arms but means go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright sunny conditions are the classic picture of fine weather.

clue.text: New positions taken after one sets examples

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
stances are positions or postures

explanation.surface: Fresh postures adopted after someone sets a lead for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken after one' places N plus STANCES after I; 'sets' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances are cases or occurrences cited as illustrations.

clue.text: Disconnected phone an urgent matter?

explanation.surface: A phone that has stopped working is a pressing problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A line that is dead has no dial tone; a time limit for finishing work is a pressing cut-off.

clue.text: Suffered having debts, harbouring scoundrel

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering within, so one piece is inside the other

parts.note: in the red means overdrawn, in debt
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A debtor shelters a rogue and pays for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' sets the scoundrel inside the debt phrase; 'Suffered' is the definition, in the sense of sustaining a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to sustain it, so the past tense means sustained.

clue.text: Flower shape fixed in the memory?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: rote is memorising by repetition, as in learning by rote
set means fixed, firm

explanation.surface: A floral pattern stuck firmly in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the fixed piece within the memory piece; the surface reads as one phrase about memorising, but 'the memory' means learning by repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rose-like arrangement, as of ribbon or petals.

clue.text: Religious adherent to observe following standard

indicators.note: following means coming after the other piece

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: A devout follower keeps watch in line with the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: A Parsee is a Zoroastrian of Indian descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsees follow Zoroastrianism, so each is a believer in that faith.

clue.text: A man is foremost in taunting a follower of Democritus

parts.note: Tom is a man's name

indicators.note: foremost means first, so the leading letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A fellow leads the mocking of a Greek philosopher's disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: Democritus was the ancient Greek thinker who held that everything is made of tiny indivisible particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Democritus taught that matter is made of indivisible particles; his followers held that theory.

clue.text: The place to be of late?

definitions.text: The place to be of late?

parts.words: The place to be of late?
parts.note: 'the late' are the dead, so the place for someone recently deceased is where bodies are kept

explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary is where bodies of the recently dead are kept before burial.

clue.text: King devours poet

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
devours means eats

explanation.surface: A monarch gobbles up a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Change suitable to be applied to notice

indicators.note: applied to means attached next to the other piece

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: Fitting alterations are made to a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to modify or alter for a new use.

clue.text: Old bird to rage about end of favourite toiletry?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pieces go round the letter

parts.note: the dodo is an extinct bird

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

parts.note: to rant is to rage

explanation.surface: An elderly bird rages about the end of a favourite bathroom product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the last letter of 'favourite' just after the first letter of the extinct-bird-plus-rage run; 'Old bird' is one piece, the extinct bird, not old plus a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A product applied to the body to mask odour is a staple of the bathroom cabinet.

clue.text: New electrical safety procedure's a risky business

parts.note: earthing is connecting a circuit to the ground for safety

explanation.surface: A new wiring safety step is a dangerous undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'procedure's' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or close call is something that nearly went wrong.

clue.text: As a precaution cut down South Americans

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: in case means as a precaution

explanation.surface: Someone trims something just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' drops the last letter E from IN CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people ruled an empire in the Andes of South America.

clue.text: Alleged clairvoyant well off, in relative terms?

definitions.text: Alleged clairvoyant well off, in relative terms?

parts.words: Alleged clairvoyant well off, in relative terms?
parts.note: folklore credits second sight to the last of seven brothers whose father was likewise the last of seven, a fortune described in family terms

explanation.definitionFit: Folklore says such a child is born with second sight and healing powers.
